quick.summary: Stop writing massive paragraphs. Format your text so busy people can act on it.
quick.takeaway: Use bullet points and bold text to help readers find the most important facts.

parts.title: Write for the scanner

beats.line: I wrote a huge document on model safety. Why did nobody read it?
Think of a person holding a long grocery list.
They want to find the milk, grab it, and leave.
Right. They do not want to read a novel in the dairy aisle.
Your readers are rushing through a store. They scan for the milk.
Your writing needs high information density.
Can I just say getting to the point?
Yes. Getting to the point helps people take action fast.
But my safety document has five crucial steps. How do I format that?

parts.cliff: Find out how to structure your text for busy readers.

beats.line: Break your wall of text into smaller blocks.
Like turning huge paragraphs into a list of bullet points?
Exactly. Bullets give the eye a safe place to land.
Make the first few words of every bullet bold.
Because the eye naturally jumps to the heavy text?
Yes. It creates a map of the most important facts.
So if they only read the bold words, they still get it.
You got it. Put the heavy lifting on the format.
First step, run the test. Second step, check the log.
Perfect. Now they will actually read your safety rules.

quiz.question: How should you format a long technical update so people actually read it?
options: Write a compelling story with a big reveal at the end.
Use bullet points and make the first few words bold.
Remove all the technical details to make it shorter.
quiz.explanation: Breaking text into bullets and bolding the main points gives the eye a place to land, making the document scannable.

quiz.question: Most readers scan a document for the facts they need instead of reading every word.
quiz.explanation: Busy professionals scan for exactly what they need to grab and take action on, instead of reading word for word.
